# Dropbeam

> Dropbeam sends files straight between your own devices, over a direct
> connection in the browser. Nothing is uploaded: there is no account, no
> server and no third-party request. The bytes travel over a WebRTC data
> channel on your local network and are checked with SHA-256 on arrival.

Dropbeam is a static web app: the whole thing is one page, it installs as a
PWA, and it works offline. Two devices pair with a QR code, a link or a
pasted code, compare three verification words, and then move files and notes
to each other.

- [Privacy and the threat model](https://github.com/sinzo8771-prog/Dropbeam/blob/main/docs/PRIVACY.md): what is stored, what leaves the device, and the tests that hold it there.

## Notes

- There is no server-side API. Every route lives in the page, and file bytes
  pass through nothing but the two browsers talking to each other.
- The optional "Across networks" setting turns on a public STUN server, which
  sees your public address. It is off by default.
- The project is MIT licensed; `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` lists the libraries
  the bundle ships.
